newsitem.title: USA: Honda sees higher '97 U.S. sales.
newsitem.headline: Honda sees higher '97 U.S. sales.

text.p: Sales this year from Honda Motor Co Ltd's Honda division in the U.S. could hit 780,000 units, higher than the all-time record of 735,920 set in 1996, Honda division senior vice president Dick Colliver said on Wednesday.

Speaking at the North American International Auto Show, Colliver said Honda expects to sell 50,000 to 60,000 of its new CR-V small sport/utilities. The vehicle goes on sale February 15 with a starting price of $19,300.

The 1997 CR-V is the first Honda-designed and engineered sport/utility. It comes equipped with a 2.0 liter dual overhead camshaft engine capable of 126 horsepower. Colliver said he expects to sell all of the CR-Vs he can get without taking away from sales of existing models.
"It should be all plus business for us," he said.

Honda expects to export 85,000 cars from the U.S. this year, up from 82,000 in 1996. Colliver said the company is also exploring whether to export more Civic cars to the U.S. from Japan because supplies of the popular vehicles are so tight.
At the end of December, Honda dealers had a 30 days' supply of cars on their lots. The industry considers 60 days to be ideal.
This fall, Honda plans to introduce a new version of its popular Accord sedan, which was the second-best selling car in American in 1996.
